source_name: Биро за јавни набавки (БЈН) — Водич за негативни референци
why_relevant: Defines the legal mechanics and location of the negative-reference (de-facto blacklist) register — required to interpret and correctly harvest the exclusion list of economic operators.

source_name: UJP internal procurement procedure document (Процедура за планирање, спроведување и реализација на јавните набавки во УЈП)
why_relevant: Reveals UJP's internal buying workflow, timelines and which unit drafts specifications — useful for timing engagement and for knowing which documents exist and can be FOI-requested.

source_name: ДКЖЈН годишни извештаи (annual reports of the Appeals Commission)
why_relevant: Annual reports aggregate appeal volumes by contracting authority and by subject of procurement, plus outcome statistics (annulled vs upheld awards). Gives a fast structural read of which public buyers of financial/payment services are most litigated, and a stable yearly time series for trend work.

source_name: e-Пазар (ePazar) — electronic marketplace for small-value procurement
why_relevant: Below-threshold purchases (small POS/card-reader batches, receipt paper, terminal maintenance, small software licences) run through the e-Pazar module rather than full open procedures, so a register built only from open tenders systematically misses this long tail. The BJN user manuals document the module's structure and access path.

source_name: BJN Прирачник за користење на ЕСЈН за економски оператори (ESJN user manual)
why_relevant: Documents the ESJN data model — notice types, dossier structure, search filters, statuses — which is exactly the schema a scraper must mirror. Cheapest way to design a robust collector without reverse-engineering the UI blindly.

source_name: Академија за судии и јавни обвинители — public procurement training materials
why_relevant: Judicial training decks on public procurement explain, in practitioner language, how ДКЖЈН and the Administrative Court actually reason about appeals — evaluation criteria, grounds for annulment, evidentiary standards. Materially improves parsing and classification of decision texts.

source_name: Pari.com.mk — fintech/licensing coverage (Paysera Macedonia first licensed EMI)
why_relevant: Business-press reporting names licensees and their launch plans faster than registers are updated, and often mentions the technology partner or platform behind a launch — the closest thing to visible procurement in a market where private PSPs publish no tenders.

source_name: Bank Western Union / MoneyGram agent pages (Stopanska, Komercijalna, Sparkasse, TTK)
why_relevant: Remittance in MK is still distributed through bank agent networks rather than standalone licensed remitters. These pages map which global remittance network is tied to which local agent — i.e. who owns the counter technology and where a non-bank remittance licensee would have to displace an incumbent.

source_name: NBRSM — Decision on issuing licences/approvals to PI and EMI and on keeping the registers
why_relevant: The bylaw that defines the exact fields kept in the public registers — tells us in advance which data points (services authorised, agents, branches) will be machine-extractable for actor mapping.

source_name: Law on Payment Services and Payment Systems (Закон за платежни услуги и платни системи, consolidated text PDF)
why_relevant: The PSD2/EMD2-aligned statute (Off. Gazette 90/2022, in force 2023) that created the licensed non-bank payments layer. Defines the service categories (PIS, AIS, acquiring, remittance, e-money) that map one-to-one onto distinct technology procurement needs.

source_name: World Bank ECA brief — Advancing the Modernization and Integration of Payment Systems in the Western Balkans
why_relevant: Names the donor-funded payments workstream (SEPA alignment, instant payments) that generates the consultancies and system procurements this cell tracks; a reliable early indicator of forthcoming TA and tenders involving the National Bank of North Macedonia.

source_name: Faktor.mk — business/tech news (vendor-bank implementation stories)
why_relevant: Carries vendor-supplied 'successful implementation at bank X' PR in Macedonian — often the only public record of an integrator's bank win.

source_name: MKD.mk — fintech coverage (Flex Pay e-money licence)
why_relevant: Documents a second EMI licensee (Флекс пеј), confirming a widening licensed layer. Mainstream media items are the earliest public trace of a new payments buyer entering the market.

source_name: ProCredit group sister-bank tender pages (Georgia/Ukraine) as template
why_relevant: Concrete evidence of what a ProCredit bank tenders for (loan origination systems, penetration testing) and how it words its calls. Gives the vocabulary and the shape of any MK-entity call, and reveals the group's shortlisted vendor universe.

source_name: ProCredit Bank Georgia — Tenders section (regional sibling procurement pattern)
why_relevant: ProCredit group subsidiaries publish their own tender pages (Georgia, Ukraine observed). The tender templates, scope wording and evaluation criteria are group-standardised, so sibling-country notices reveal the specification patterns ProCredit Bank AD Skopje will use even when MK-side notices are not published.

source_name: TED / EU Publications Office notice — NBRNM coins procurement
why_relevant: Confirms NBRNM publishes above-threshold notices to EU-visible channels (a coins supply notice, CPV 18512100, 2 lots, published 05/03/2024, deadline 29/03/2024, electronic submission via e-nabavki). Gives an English-language, structured mirror of Macedonian central-bank tenders.

source_name: Meta.mk — policy reporting on e-money bylaws
why_relevant: Explains, in accessible mk, when the NBRSM bylaws opened the market and what new services became possible — a dating anchor for the licensing timeline and a source of quotes from the regulator on expected market entry.

source_name: EACHA annual conference (Skopje edition) - agenda / sponsor coverage
why_relevant: Coverage of the EACHA 2026 Skopje conference names the institutions and vendor types in the room and the themes (account-to-account digital payments, ISO alignment). Which global IT/consulting firms travel to Skopje for this is a direct read on who is positioning for MK payment-infrastructure work.

source_name: BIS CPMI Red Book — Payment, clearing and settlement systems in Macedonia
why_relevant: Independent, structured description of MIPS, KIBS and CaSys, their ownership, participants and technical arrangements. Best single English baseline for understanding who operates what before reading MK-language sources; dated but structurally reliable.

entity_name: International vendor press-release wires covering MK bank wins
source_name: International vendor press-release wires covering MK bank wins (e.g. Entrust / BCS North Macedonia at Komercijalna banka)
why_relevant: Global vendors announce MK deals on international wires before or instead of MK media - here Entrust with local partner BCS North Macedonia delivering card digitisation and push provisioning to Google Wallet at Komercijalna banka. These releases name the local implementation partner, which is exactly the actor set that bids on subsequent tenders, and a wallet/tokenisation win at one bank reliably precedes peer-bank projects.

source_name: Interoperable Europe Portal — NIFO country factsheet, North Macedonia
why_relevant: Annual EU factsheet describing North Macedonia's interoperability platform, e-services and digital-government governance. Excellent context/actor map and identifies capability gaps that translate into future procurement.

source_name: Karanovic & Partners — North Macedonia payments law commentary (EN)
why_relevant: Regional law-firm client alerts in English explain the 2022 Law on Payment Services and Payment Systems and its EU-harmonised consequences. English-language bridge that decodes the Macedonian regulatory vocabulary used in the local press.

source_name: MicroBalkans 2026 (regional financial-sector conference, Skopje)
why_relevant: Third edition of a Skopje conference drawing 200+ financial-sector representatives from 15 European countries, explicitly targeting non-bank financial institutions, microcredit institutions, savings houses, banks, fintech and IT companies, investors and regulators. Sponsor/exhibitor rosters of exactly this kind of event flag vendors courting MK buyers ahead of tenders.

source_name: Open Society Foundations Western Balkans — policy brief: Open Data and Public Procurement in North Macedonia
why_relevant: Donor/CSO policy brief (2025) assessing the actual state of open procurement data in MK — notes that after an initial wave of disclosures following Bureau recommendations, access to procurement data and spending remains limited. Gives an independent, dated quality assessment of the official data layer, which is essential for calibrating how much to trust e-nabavki-derived datasets.

source_name: SELDI corruption assessment report — Macedonia (seldi.net)
why_relevant: Regional CSO anti-corruption network assessment covering Macedonia, using the Corruption Monitoring System methodology, with quantified procurement observations (e.g. centralised procurement rising to 11% of total analysed procurement value from 4% in 2011). Provides methodology and longitudinal baselines that a purely news-driven view lacks.

source_name: Smartportal.mk — tech/product launch coverage (Pay by link, CaSys)
why_relevant: Covers first-in-market payment product launches by local suppliers; complements bankarstvo.mk for consumer-facing payment innovations.

source_name: US ITA Country Commercial Guide — North Macedonia: Selling to the Public Sector
why_relevant: Concise English overview of how the MK procurement system works for foreign vendors — thresholds, e-Nabavki mechanics, typical barriers. Good orientation document and a sanity check on the legal framework, refreshed annually.
